title: Canada Walked Out of India's Nuclear Reactor
title_alternatives: 1974: Canada Left. India Rebuilt Its Heart

description:
In 1974, Canada walked out of a half-built nuclear reactor at Rawatbhata in Rajasthan. India finished it. Twenty years later its 306 pressure tubes were wearing out, and Canada's export rules kept its firms out of the job.

This is how Indian engineers learned to open a reactor's heart and replace it themselves, from Rajasthan unit 2 to Kakrapar and India's own 700 MW reactors.

The date to watch: the day Rajasthan unit 8 goes critical.

pinned_comment:
Thank you for staying with me till the end.

You might ask me, Kishore, why spend all this effort on these reactors when India's real hope is thorium? Because India's plan has three stages, and this reactor is stage one. Reactors like this make the plutonium the fast breeder at Kalpakkam needs, and only after that can thorium be bred into fuel. No 306 tubes, no thorium.

One fact to keep: a reactor of this family at Kaiga ran 962 days without stopping, a world record.

So tell me honestly. Would you have waited for help, or opened it yourself?

And the day Rajasthan unit 8 goes critical, I want you here with me. Subscribe, so you are.
